props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions. - `unmount`: Manually unmounts the dialog. Call this after any externally controlled closing animation finishes. - `close`: Closes the dialog imperatively when called.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the dialog. This can be a regular React node or a render function that receives the `payload` of the active trigger.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the dialog is initially open.

props.name: defaultTriggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open dialog.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description: Whether to prevent the dialog from closing on outside presses. For non-modal dialogs, this also prevents the dialog from closing when focus moves outside of it.

props.name: handle
props.description: A handle to associate the dialog with a trigger. If specified, allows external triggers to control the dialog's open state. Can be created with the Dialog.createHandle() method.

props.name: modal
props.description: Determines if the dialog enters a modal state when open. - `true`: user interaction is limited to just the dialog: focus is trapped, document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled. - `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed. - `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the dialog, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Event handler called when the dialog is opened or closed.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the dialog is opened or closed.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the dialog is currently open.

props.name: triggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled dialog. There's no need to specify this prop when the dialog is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set).

props.name: bar
props.description: A pinned bar of a scrolling (`size="wide"`) dialog.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` (32px) and `icon-md` for rows, cards, banners, toolbars and panel headers; `lg` and `icon-lg` (the control height) for dialog footers, forms and beside a field; `xl` for a full-width call to action. The size follows the place: see Button › Size by place.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

name: DialogCommit
description: The dialog's one commit button: a `Button`, written where it goes on a desktop (the end of `DialogFooter`). In a `DialogSheetContent` below 768px it is drawn at the end of the sheet's head instead, the same button (color, words, disabled and loading state) at `size="md"`. In a flow of steps, write each step's button as one (Next, then the last step's action).

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: shows the spinner and blocks activation (click, Enter, Space and form submission) while keeping the button focusable. A busy button is `aria-disabled`, not natively `disabled`, so the focus a press left on it stays there and is still there when the wait ends.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: The spinner's accessible name while `loading`: say what is happening.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` (32px) and `icon-md` for rows, cards, banners, toolbars and panel headers; `lg` and `icon-lg` (the control height) for dialog footers, forms and beside a field; `xl` for a full-width call to action. The size follows the place: see Button › Size by place.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where the card sits in the window. `"center"` (the default): in the middle. `"top"`: centred across, its top edge at `var(--dialog-top, 8vh)`, and never taller than the window less that top and 16px, so it never runs past the window's bottom; its width is still `size`'s. To anchor the card to something on the page (search under the top bar's field), measure it and set `--dialog-top` in `style`. Below 768px the card stays centred and moves up to that top only while the on-screen keyboard is open, so the keyboard doesn't cover it (dialog.md, "On a phone").

props.description: Determines the element to focus when the dialog is opened. By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the dialog is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard.

props.name: actionsRef
props.type: ((instance: ScrollAreaActions | null) => void | (() => void | { [UNDEFINED_VOID_ONLY]: never; }) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<ScrollAreaActions | null>
props.description: Methods to scroll from code that the container doesn't have natively.

props.name: children
props.description: The scrolling content, in ScrollArea's own container.

props.name: contentRef
props.description: An element whose size is the content's, watched for size changes (such as a hidden mirror of a textarea's text). Without it each element child of the container is watched, and children added or removed.

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Style of the content element; renders it, as `contentClassName` does.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade the content out toward an edge that has more past it. The scrollbars don't fade.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the scrollbars stay after scrolling stops, in ms. At least 100 with `trigger="scroll"`.

props.name: onEdgeChange
props.description: Called when the area reaches or leaves an edge, and after mounting when the content overflows.

props.name: onScroll
props.description: The container's scroll events.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The directions the area scrolls in. Content too wide for a vertical area is cut off.

props.name: overscroll
props.description: What a scroll that reaches the end does: stop there with no bounce (`none`, the default), stop there but let Mac trackpads and iOS bounce the area (`contain`), or carry on to the page behind (`auto`, which leaves the container's own `overscroll-behavior` alone). Only in the directions the area overflows right now.

props.name: railInset
props.description: Room in px the scrollbars keep clear at each end, such as a sticky header's height, so they don't run over it. Also settable in CSS, on the root: `--r-scroll-area-rail-inset-{top,bottom,left,right}`, which don't inherit.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element in place of ScrollArea's own `<div>`, as the container (an element or a function that gets the props). It must hold children: the gutters are its first child.

props.name: size
props.description: Thumb thickness: `small` is 5px, `medium` 7px; both grow while pointed at or dragged.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: The container's: by default `0` while there is something to scroll.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the scrollbars show. They always show while scrolling or dragging.

props.name: forceRender
props.description: Whether the backdrop is forced to render even when nested.

name: DialogSheetBack
description: Back, in a later step of a flow drawn as a phone sheet: it takes the head's start in place of × (stdrc, 2026-10-22). The sheet is a stack of steps, and Back undoes one, as on a pushed page; Esc still closes. Put it in `DialogHeader` beside the `DialogClose`, from the second step on; it draws nothing outside a sheet, where Back stays in the footer. Its icon is `arrow-left`, as every Back (Alignment, "The ends of a header").

props.name: activateOnTouchEnd
props.description: Activate when the finger lifts instead of on the click after it, so a tap that stops a scrolling page still acts. Give it to Back, the header's navigation; not to actions that change things (design/patterns/navigation.md#switching-on-finger-lift).

name: DialogSheetContent
description: DialogContent for a dialog with several fields, a long list or steps. On a desktop and a tablet it is DialogContent, the same DOM and classes. Below 768px it is a sheet: docked to the bottom, 90% of the screen tall, sliding up over its scrim; `DialogHeader` becomes a pushed page's head (× at the start, the title, the `DialogCommit` button at the end), `DialogFooter` is hidden (× is Cancel) and `DialogBody` scrolls on the phone's 16px margin above the home indicator. Base UI keeps Esc, focus and close. `placement` applies on a desktop and a tablet only: the sheet is docked to the bottom.

props.description: Where the card sits in the window. `"center"` (the default): in the middle. `"top"`: centred across, its top edge at `var(--dialog-top, 8vh)`, and never taller than the window less that top and 16px, so it never runs past the window's bottom; its width is still `size`'s. To anchor the card to something on the page (search under the top bar's field), measure it and set `--dialog-top` in `style`. Below 768px the card stays centred and moves up to that top only while the on-screen keyboard is open, so the keyboard doesn't cover it (dialog.md, "On a phone").

name: DialogSurface
description: The dialog's frame — the popover layer, the dialog radius, the seam ring and the float shadow — for a centred modal whose lifecycle the app owns (its own backdrop, Escape and focus handling). It neither positions nor animates itself: the host centres it, and a centred modal has no motion. DialogContent draws the same frame for a Base UI dialog.

name: DialogFooterNote
description: One short line at the start of `DialogFooter` that says what the commit button will do ("You'll be billed $8 per member each month"). Muted footnote text, start-aligned and never cut. Only in a `lg` or `wide` dialog, and at most 40 characters: on a desktop it is one line beside the buttons and never wraps; on a phone it goes above the buttons when they don't fit beside it, and may wrap to 2 lines. In a phone sheet, which has no footer, it moves to the end of the body. Longer copy belongs in the body. A footer holds a note or a `TextLink`, never both.
